title: Curved mirrors
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: A shiny spoon (both sides), a car side mirror, a torch reflector and a make-up mirror. Ray diagrams are drawn with a ruler on squared paper; the drawing is marked by the teacher and the rules and results are tested here.

skills.key_step: The child names the types of curved mirrors (concave curves inwards and brings light together; convex curves outwards and spreads it) and describes the images: convex always small, upright and virtual; concave depends on the distance.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the image in a plane mirror.
floor.question: Is the image in a plane mirror the same size as the object?

representations: a car side mirror and a make-up mirror
steps: Concave: like the inside of a spoon or a cave.
Convex: like the back of a spoon.
Convex image: small, upright, virtual, always.
Concave image: large and upright close up; inverted far away.

board.do: Draw a mirror curving in and one curving out.

board.say: What does your face look like in this one?

misconceptions.ask: Which is like the mouth of a cave?
Which side of the spoon bulges out?
How big did you look in the back of the spoon?
misconceptions.repair: Convex gives small, upright, virtual images.

misconceptions.ask: What happened when you held the spoon far away?
misconceptions.repair: Far from a concave mirror the image is inverted.

checks.question: Which mirror always forms a small, upright image?
Which side of a spoon acts as a concave mirror?

skills.key_step: The child applies the ray rules (a ray parallel to the axis reflects through F, or away from it for convex; a ray through C reflects back on itself) with two rays, and states where the image forms and what it is like.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the two kinds of curved mirror.
floor.question: Which mirror curves inwards?

representations: squared paper, a ruler and a drawn mirror with C and F marked
a torch beam on a spoon bowl
a results table by object position
steps: Mark the principal axis, F and C.
Ray 1: parallel to the axis, reflected through F.
Ray 2: through C, reflected straight back.
Where they meet is the image; describe it.

board.do: Draw a concave mirror with C and F on the axis and an object beyond C.
Draw the ray parallel to the axis.
Ask where this ray goes after reflection.
Ask the child to draw the ray through C and mark the image.

misconceptions.ask: Where could a single ray end?
misconceptions.repair: Two rays meet at the image.

misconceptions.ask: Where did the torch beam gather?
misconceptions.repair: A parallel ray reflects through F.

listen_for: a convex mirror gives a real image
misconceptions.ask: Do the reflected rays from a convex mirror meet in front?
misconceptions.repair: Convex images are virtual, behind the mirror.

misconceptions.ask: What did you see with the spoon very close?
misconceptions.repair: Between F and the mirror: upright, larger, virtual.

checks.question: In a concave mirror, where does a ray parallel to the principal axis go after reflection?
An object is beyond C in front of a concave mirror. Describe its image.
checks.answer: real, inverted, smaller, between F and C

skills.key_step: The child says where concave mirrors are used (shaving and make-up mirrors, dentist mirrors, torch and headlamp reflectors, solar cookers) and convex mirrors (vehicle side mirrors, shop and road-bend security mirrors) and why.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the images curved mirrors form.
floor.question: What image does a convex mirror form?

representations: a car mirror and a torch reflector
steps: Need a big image close up: concave.
Need a beam or to gather sunlight: concave.
contexts: a solar cooker in a school

board.do: Draw a road bend with a mirror on a pole.
Ask the child to add a concave mirror use.

misconceptions.ask: What does a driver need to see?
misconceptions.repair: Driving mirrors are convex for a wide view.

misconceptions.ask: How did your face look close to the spoon bowl?
What does a guard need to see?
What shape is the torch reflector?

checks.question: Why are convex mirrors used as vehicle side mirrors?
checks.answer: they give a wide field of view

checks.question: Give one use of a concave mirror.
checks.answer: shaving or make-up mirror, dentist mirror, torch reflector, solar cooker
